intended_scope: Robot cells, conveyors, PLCs, HMIs, sensors, drives, and line-control contexts common in discrete production environments, while keeping detailed execution sequencing and MES product genealogy outside the profile scaffold.
measurement_signal_expectations: Motor current, speed, cycle, position, and sensor state should preserve typed measurement semantics where queried frequently.
Controller or gateway identifiers should remain traceable across migrations.
event_alarm_expectations: Drive faults, communication loss, interlocks, and suppression windows should remain explicit.
Event-to-alarm-to-recommendation flow should remain distinguishable from operator work history.
reliability_work_requirements: Work outcomes should distinguish successful restoration from inconclusive resets.
Recommendations and actions should remain linked to the cell or asset context they affect.

safety_cyber_applicability.safety_profile_applicability: Applicable where guarding, interlocks, or safety controllers participate in cell context.
safety_cyber_applicability.cyber_profile_applicability: Applicable for PLC, HMI, drive, and gateway zone or conduit context.
notes: Discrete safety context is bounded to operational traceability, not complete machine-safety engineering.
Cyber context is bounded to foundational identity and topology semantics.

servicenow_serving_projection_implicatio: Project line or cell operational state, anomalies, drive faults, and workflow references.
Do not project raw sensor streams or every transition into workflow-primary storage.
known_exclusions: Full MES schedule, job, and genealogy modeling.
Detailed robot program, motion path, or PLC logic definitions.

end_to_end_example.scenario_label: Robot cell drive fault and workflow escalation
end_to_end_example.narrative_summary: A robot cell contains a PLC, HMI, and VFD. A drive fault becomes an alarm and recommendation, is evaluated for cyber and workflow context, and is projected into a workflow-facing surface without losing topology meaning.

stages.summary: The cell preserves measurement context for drive and sensor observations.
A VFD fault event leads to a governed alarm and recommendation.
Recommended maintenance or reset work remains distinct from outcome claims.
The VFD and PLC remain visible as cyber-managed devices within zone and conduit context.
A curated workflow projection exposes risk, active anomalies, and related assets for system-of-action routing.
The cell retains topology and evidence lineage for later verification and recurrence analysis.
